1.  COMMENDATIONS: ENVIRONMENTAL SCHOLARSHIP AWARD RECIPIENTS – F2M25-3

  Mayor Lee and City Council wished to commend the recent winners of the Fourth Annual
  Environmental Scholarship Award. Republic Services joined with the City of Alhambra to
  award five scholarships of $1,000 to Alhambra students. Each finalist submitted an essay

  C.  FY 2025-2026 Appropriation Limit: Proposition XIII B (Gann Initiative) prohibits local
  agencies from exceeding their 1978-79 fiscal year appropriations after allowing for
  cost-of-living (CPI) and population changes which are certified by the State
  Department of Finance. Proposition 111 allows the City to adjust its annual limits for
  the following factors, subject to approval by the City Council:
  a)  Either the California Per Capita Income or the percentage change in local
  assessment roll from the preceding year due to the addition of local nonresidential
  construction in the City.
  b)  Either the City’s own population growth or the population growth of the entire
  county.

  Government Code Section 7910 requires agencies to adopt a resolution each year
  disclosing their appropriation limit. In accordance with Proposition 111, the City is
  required to conduct a review of their appropriations limit during the annual financial
  audit. For fiscal year 2023-2024, the City’s appropriation limit was reviewed by our
  auditors, Moss, Levy & Hartzheim, LLP, and determined to be properly calculated. The
  calculations in computing the City of Alhambra’s appropriation limit for the 2025-2026
  fiscal year are on file in the Finance Department. The appropriation limit for the 2025-
  26 fiscal year was $201,962,521 and the applicable appropriation subject to this
  limitation was $85,928,695. Therefore, the City was favorably under the appropriations
  limit by $116,033,826.

  change +.22%) used in the calculation of the appropriation limit.

 4.  RIDERSHIP TRANSPORTATION STUDY FOR THE ALHAMBRA COMMUNITY TRANSIT
  (ACT) – F2M23-16

  Deputy Director of Transportation for Public Works CHAN delivered a staff report. In January
  2025, City staff contracted Kimley-Horn to conduct a Ridership Transportation Study for the
  Alhambra Community Transit (ACT). Zander DALLY, the Transit Planning Analyst at Kimley-
  Horn, provided a presentation, which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. The study included an
  assessment of the existing transit market, an analysis of ridership and operations, and
  engagement with stakeholders and riders. The study evaluated ACT’s current fixed-route
  system and found that while much of the City was within a half mile of transit, areas in South
  Alhambra are underserved and ACT’s Blue Line was underutilized in these sections. Surveys
  and operator input revealed demand for service to specific destinations not currently served,
  including Atlantic Times Square, Granada Park, and Garfield Avenue. Based on route
  performance and surveys, the study recommended implementing Revenue Neutral Alternative
  (Option B), which would modify the Blue and Green Lines to better serve underserved areas
  while increasing ridership and maintaining current operating costs. Under this alternative, the
  Blue Line would be altered to serve Garfield Avenue and Hellman Avenue, while also providing
  enhanced coverage of east Alhambra. The Green Line was slightly modified only in the
  clockwise direction, while the counter-clockwise route remained unchanged. Revenue Neutral
  Alternative (Option B) was projected to increase Blue Line ridership by approximately 44%
  and Green Line ridership by about 6%, marking the largest increase among all the service
  alternatives considered. Staff worked closely with First Transit, the City’s transit operations
  contractor, and they agreed to the proposed route improvements without additional operating
  costs to the City. The new service was expected to begin by the end of the calendar year. The
  proposed route recommendations were budget neutral. Ms. CHAN discussed the next steps
  of the process.

  Public Comment:
  1) Shirley TATSUNO, 1408 S. Fifth St., spoke in support of the expansion of bus services but
  suggested increased bus arrivals to further encourage ridership. She requested more
  information regarding the bus routes during the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. She further spoke

  previous discussions of a no-fee alternative program and supported consideration of this
  alternative. He went on to discuss the importance of local public transportation.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor MALONEY supported the survey and continued to discuss for a
  non-revenue neutral service with Mr. DALLY. Mr. DALLY explained the enhanced service
  alternative which was previously proposed, but not included in the current recommendations.
  Ms. CHAN explained the projected costs associated with the enhanced service alternative as
  well as the projected ridership. Mr. MALONEY stated that he supported moving forward with

6.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: PARKING ENFORCEMENT SERVICES – F2M21-23, C2M21-
  21, M2M25-79

  The current agreement with Inter-Con Security Systems for parking enforcement services
  expires June 30, 2026. Staff reached out to Inter-Con Security Systems to add Automated
  License Plate Recognition (ALPR) to the Inter-Con vehicles to maximize efficiency when
  running license plates and matching them with overnight permits. The service would cost an
  additional $64,931.40 for FY 25/26 and $52,290.41 for FY 26/27. However, the cost was
  expected to be offset by increased parking citation revenues resulting from expanded parking
  enforcement coverage. Staff recommended amending the contract to add the cost of the
  ALPRs to vehicles. In addition, staff requested to extend the contract for an additional four
  years through June 30, 2030, aligning with the City’s parking citation system contract. Staff
  recommended dispensing with the competitive bidding process under Municipal Code Section
  3.38.050 to avoid operational disruptions.
